sentences.text: Chucarosaurus was an extinct genus of titanosaurian dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Early Cretaceous. This large creature possessed slender limbs.
The genus contains only one known species, C. diripienda, which is known from limb and pelvic bones. The femur of this dinosaur was roughly 1.9 meters long.

The genus and species Chucarosaurus diripienda were described by Agnolin et al. in 2023. The holotype specimen was discovered at the Pueblo Blanco Natural Reserve in Río Negro Province, Argentina, within the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous. The holotype specimen consists of various limb and pelvic bones belonging to a single individual.
The Huincul Formation also yielded fossils of diverse dinosaurs including titanosaurs, abelisaurids, carcharodontosaurids, and avetheropods.
Chucarosaurus is classified as a colossosaurian member of the Titanosauria, closely related to a clade containing Notocolossus and the Lognkosauria.
Chucarosaurus lived in the Early Cretaceous Huincul Formation of Río Negro Province, Argentina. Chucarosaurus lived between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago during the Albian stage.
